source.title: Robust Noisy Label Learning via Two-Stream Sample Distillation
source.authors: Sihan Bai; Sanping Zhou; Zheng Qin; Le Wang; Nanning Zheng

record.tranche_reason: Reports classification accuracy across noisy-label rates, bearing on the test-accuracy part of V4, but uses a noisy-label-learning method rather than the original random-label fitting measurement.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for symmetric and asymmetric label noise, but does not report training error on those settings. Its cited discussion of memorization is prior work, not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The study uses the memorization effect to motivate small-loss sample selection and evaluates a mitigation method for noisy labels. Its results measure test accuracy and sample-selection quality, without measuring fitting of the original noisy training labels or learning order for clean versus noisy labels. These results do not test V4's joint claim of perfect training fit and degrading generalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that combining loss-space and feature-space selection with meta sample purification improves clean-sample identification and noisy-label classification across four datasets. They do not establish random-label fitting or clean-before-noise learning dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a two-stream sample-distillation framework for noisy-label learning, with semi-supervised training; it does not apply the original random-label fitting experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported classification accuracy varies across datasets and label-noise rates; Table I also shows a discrepancy for CIFAR-100 at 80% symmetric noise between Tables I and IV.

fits_no_version.finding: TSSD test accuracy generally decreases as label corruption increases, while its performance usually exceeds competing noisy-label-learning methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-stream sample selection and semi-supervised training improve classification robustness under label noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Sample-selection F1 improves and stabilizes during training; MSP increases the cleanliness of selected uncertain samples by approximately 10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-space and feature-space information can improve identification of clean labels during noisy-label mitigation.

record.problems: No training-error results are reported for the noisy-label settings. Tables I and II are flattened in the supplied text, and Table I's CIFAR-100 result at 80% symmetric noise differs from Table IV.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows were extracted. Table III reports Clothing-1M performance for real-world noisy labels without a stated corruption fraction, so it does not measure the noise-rate progression named in V4.

untested.parts: Fitting completely random labels to near-zero training error with unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters, and chance test performance.
Relative time to fit true versus random labels and convergence slowing with increasing corruption.
Perfect training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect fit of original noisy training labels alongside steadily increasing test error through complete randomization. TSSD filters and refines labels and treats rejected labels as unlabeled; its test accuracy alone does not establish this behavior.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevents random-label fitting, and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Learning shared real-data patterns before memorizing noisy labels. Figure 8 tracks sample-selection F1, not separate learning trajectories for real and noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: The reported accuracy values are method-performance outcomes and should not serve as evidence rows for V1–V6. The cited memorization result is prior work. No additional claim-bearing results require extraction.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling result or test error at chance is reported.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label-noise rates is reported.
No shuffled-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiments are reported.
The paper reports test classification accuracy at multiple noisy-label rates, but does not report whether training error remains zero or how it changes with noise.
No experiment tests whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation affects fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
The paper cites the memorization effect but does not test learning order for real versus noisy labels.
